mechanism_narrative: A four-week rise in WORKPLACES from -12.4 to -10.7 signals returning commuting routines that increase weekday retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -12.4 to -10.7 across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues rising but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT crosses above -35 percent of baseline, it marks a mobility-normalization threshold that pulls discretionary trips back to retail venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -35 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -37.4 at t-2w to -34.4 at t-0w, crossing -35
failure_condition: If TRANSIT is above -35 for at least one week and RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than or equal to its last 14-day mean, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL from 7.7 to 4.6 and rising WORKPLACES from -12.4 to -10.7 interact: people are leaving home for work and errands, jointly increasing retail-and-recreation exposure over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5 and WORKPLACES rises above -11
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.7 to 4.6 while WORKPLACES rose from -12.4 to -10.7
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL is below 5 and WORKPLACES above -11 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently deep negative PARKS values reflect cool, wet early-spring conditions that suppress outdoor leisure and spillover retail trips, keeping RETAIL_REC below its recent four-week mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below -33 while RESIDENTIAL remains above 4.5
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is -35.0 and RESIDENTIAL is 4.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS remains below -33 and RESIDENTIAL above 4.5 but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM near +1.6 to +1.9 shows no renewed stockpiling or panic buying, freeing household movement for discretionary retail, so RETAIL_REC rises within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains between 1.5 and 2.0 for three consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM readings are 1.9, 1.6, 1.9, 1.6 over the four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays within 1.5 to 2.0 but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than its last 7-day mean, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Easing capacity rules allow TRANSIT and WORKPLACES to recover together, and their interaction amplifies retail-and-recreation visits over the next two weeks more than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 1 point week-on-week while WORKPLACES rises more than 0.5 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -37.4 to -34.4 and WORKPLACES rose from -12.4 to -10.7
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than its last 14-day mean, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In an ongoing reopening regime, TRANSIT recovery from -37.4 to -34.4 pulls retail trips back toward baseline, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks even if WORKPLACES stalls.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved by 3.0 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues improving but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A continued fall in RESIDENTIAL below 4.6 means fewer people are staying home, which mechanically increases time spent in retail-and-recreation venues and raises RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 7.7 at t-3w to 4.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls below 4.6 but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than its last 7-day mean, this hypothesis is rejected.
